---
title: "Speed & Power on 60-Foot Bases"
subtitle: "Why Most Standout Hitters Pick Either Home Runs or Stolen Bases—and the Few Who Do Both"
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

prep_standouts <- \(df, yr) {
  df |>
    mutate(Season = yr) |>
    filter(HR >= 10 | SB >= 15) |>
    mutate(
      Attempts = SB + CS,
      SBPct = if_else(Attempts > 0, SB / Attempts, NA_real_),
      Role = case_when(
        HR >= 10 & SB >= 15 ~ "Dual Threat (Both)",
        HR >= 10 ~ "Power (10+ HR)",
        TRUE ~ "Speed (15+ SB)"
      ),
      Role = factor(
        Role,
        levels = c(
          "Power (10+ HR)",
          "Speed (15+ SB)",
          "Dual Threat (Both)"
        )
      )
    )
}

standouts_2021 <- read_csv("batting2021.csv") |> prep_standouts(2021L)
standouts_2022 <- read_csv("batting2022.csv") |> prep_standouts(2022L)
all_standouts <- bind_rows(standouts_2021, standouts_2022)
```

In NCAA Division I softball, where bases sit just **60 feet apart**, base stealers succeed **83.5% of the time** (21,328 steals in 25,535 tries across 2021 and 2022). Yet hitting for power and stealing bases usually belong to completely different types of players.

To make that L-shaped split easy to see without thousands of low-volume bench rows cluttering the corner, the two charts below focus on college softball's **standout power and speed threats**—every player who either hit **10+ home runs** or stole **15+ bases**:

- **Blue dots (left side):** **Power Hitters** who crush 10+ home runs a year but rarely steal.
- **Green dots (bottom):** **Speed Threats**—often slap hitters—who steal 15 to 59 bases while hitting very few home runs.
- **Red dots (middle/top-right):** Rare **Dual-Threat Stars** who reach *both* 10+ home runs and 15+ stolen bases in the same season.

## 2021 Season: Speed vs. Power

```{r}
make_speed_power_plot <- \(df, plot_title) {
  p <- df |>
    arrange(Role) |>
    ggplot(aes(
      x = SB,
      y = HR,
      color = Role,
      size = Role,
      text = paste0(
        "<b>", Player, " (", Team, ")</b>",
        "<br>Role: ", Role,
        "<br>Home Runs: ", HR,
        "<br>Stolen Bases: ", SB, " (", CS, " caught",
        if_else(!is.na(SBPct), paste0(", ", round(100 * SBPct, 1), "%"), ""), ")",
        "<br>Batting Avg: ", sprintf("%.3f", BA), " | OPS: ", sprintf("%.3f", OPS)
      )
    )) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 15, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray60") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Power (10+ HR)" = "#1d4ed8",
        "Speed (15+ SB)" = "#059669",
        "Dual Threat (Both)" = "#dc2626"
      ),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_size_manual(
      values = c(
        "Power (10+ HR)" = 2.3,
        "Speed (15+ SB)" = 2.3,
        "Dual Threat (Both)" = 3.5
      ),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = "Stolen Bases (SB)",
      y = "Home Runs (HR)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text", height = 450) |>
    layout(
      margin = list(t = 60, b = 90, l = 60, r = 25),
      legend = list(
        orientation = "h",
        x = 0.5,
        xanchor = "center",
        y = -0.22
      )
    )
}

make_speed_power_plot(
  standouts_2021,
  "2021 Standout Threats: Power (10+ HR) vs. Speed (15+ SB)"
)
```

In 2021 (331 standout hitters), notice how cleanly the blue and green dots separate along the two axes: Oklahoma's **Jocelyn Alo** sits high on the left (34 HRs, 0 SBs), while Central Arkansas's **Jenna Wildeman** stretches all the way to the right along zero (0 HRs, 56 SBs). Only **13 players** in the country reached the red dual-threat zone, led by Miami (OH)'s **Karli Spaid** (17 HRs, 19 SBs) and Eastern Illinois's **Megan Burton** (19 HRs, 17 SBs).

## 2022 Season: Speed vs. Power

```{r}
make_speed_power_plot(
  standouts_2022,
  "2022 Standout Threats: Power (10+ HR) vs. Speed (15+ SB)"
)
```

In 2022 (433 standout hitters), the dual-threat group grew to **16 players**—highlighted by Wichita State's **Addison Barnard**, who sits way up in the top middle with **33 home runs and 25 stolen bases**, alongside Northwestern's **Rachel Lewis** (23 HRs, 25 SBs) and Tennessee's **Kiki Milloy** (15 HRs, 31 SBs). Meanwhile, USF speedster **Alexis Johns** pushed pure base stealing even further on the bottom right with **59 steals in 61 tries** and zero home runs.

## The Elite 15 HR / 15 SB Club (2021–2022)

Raise the bar to **at least 15 home runs and 15 stolen bases** in a single season, and only **7 player-seasons out of 4,406** across both years made the cut:

```{r}
club_15_15 <- all_standouts |>
  filter(HR >= 15, SB >= 15) |>
  arrange(desc(OPS)) |>
  transmute(
    Player,
    College = Team,
    Season,
    HR,
    `SB-CS` = paste0(SB, "-", CS),
    `SB%` = paste0(round(100 * SBPct, 1), "%"),
    BA = sprintf("%.3f", BA),
    OBP = sprintf("%.3f", OBP),
    OPS = sprintf("%.3f", OPS)
  )

knitr::kable(club_15_15, align = c("l", "l", "c", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))
```
